turns.en: Amazing. For someone that maybe doesn't have a Christian around as a coach or a manager that isn't at this level, what advice do you give people that are looking for a coach or someone that could help them along these lines to learn to build trust and learn to just generally improve?
turns.zh: 惊人的。对于那些可能没有基督徒作为教练或经理的人来说，他们没有达到这个级别，对于那些正在寻找教练或可以帮助他们学习建立信任并学习总体改进的人，您有什么建议？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Boy, like I say with everything, you don't get mastery by avoidance. And one of the things that good coaches do that when I say corporations fail companies is they don't create space for practice. I see people complain to me about people all the time, oh this person is not good. They presented this, it was terrible. And I ask them, "What did they do at practice?" They say, "What do you mean?" I say, "When they were practicing this, what did they do?" Say, "Well, they didn't practice. I told them to prepare this." I say, "Think about what happens at practice. Any practice of any sport, any game. You can stop. You can make corrections, you can give feedback. What you do at practice, you do in the game. Product management is a one time, game time kind of role. So when do people practice?" (01:00:57): And so what I tell people in the absence of getting good coaching, you need to find practice arenas. It's kind of like if you are learning a new sport or basketball, you kind go to the gym. It's a practice arena. You can play and shoot around and let maybe some people have pickup games that you join and stuff like this in some ways. And so I always advise product managers like, you need to join a lot of pickup games, which they are low barriers to entry, low evaluation reward, loan risk type of thing. Go volunteer at a non-profit working with the team, go volunteer in your community event or church or whatever you go to, go party. But now what am I trying to do with these things? Find places where people do collaborative problem solving. That is what you're doing as a product team. (01:01:50): It's more likely in a high performance environment you'll find a good coach. You'll find somebody out there but what you're also doing is you're observing other people play. Most people learn a lot of skills by, you watch TV like, oh I like that move. And then you go to the gym and you practice that move, you see what you do? So it's like you're seeing then you're doing it in some ways. So you need to see good product work so that you can do good product work so that you can teach good product work. So if you don't have the benefit of having a good coach directly, you've got to find environments where you see good coaching happening and a good indication of good coaching is actually good outcomes over and over again. Winning teams, winning performances, great products, great products come from great product teams. They probably have good leaders or a good leader within a bad culture.
turns.zh: 男孩，就像我对一切所说的那样，你无法通过回避来掌握。当我说企业失败时，优秀教练所做的事情之一就是他们不创造练习空间。我总是看到有人向我抱怨人，哦这个人不好。他们提出了这个，太可怕了。我问他们，“他们在训练中做了什么？”他们说：“你是什么意思？”我说：“当他们练习这个的时候，他们做了什么？”说：“好吧，他们没有练习。我告诉他们准备这个。”我说：“想想练习时会发生什么。任何运动、任何比赛的任何练习。你可以停下来。你可以进行纠正，你可以提供反馈。你在练习中所做的，你在比赛中所做的。产品管理是一种一次性的、比赛时间的角色。那么人们什么时候练习呢？” (01:00:57)：所以我告诉人们，在没有得到良好指导的情况下，你需要找到练习场地。这有点像如果你正在学习一项新的运动或篮球，你就会去健身房。这是一个练习场。你可以到处玩、射击，也许有些人可以参加你参加的临时游戏，或者以某种方式进行类似的事情。所以我总是建议产品经理，你需要加入很多皮卡游戏，它们的进入门槛低，评价奖励低，贷款风险之类的东西。与团队一起在非营利组织做志愿者，在社区活动或教堂或任何你去的地方做志愿者，参加聚会。但现在我想用这些东西做什么呢？寻找人们协作解决问题的地方。这就是你作为产品团队正在做的事情。 (01:01:50)：在高绩效环境中你更有可能找到一位好教练。你会发现有人在那里，但你也在做的就是观察其他人打球。大多数人通过看电视来学习很多技能，哦，我喜欢那个动作。然后你去健身房练习那个动作，你知道你做了什么吗？所以就像你看到你正在以某种方式做这件事一样。所以你需要看到好的产品工作，这样你才能做好产品工作，这样你才能教授好的产品工作。因此，如果你没有直接拥有一位好教练的好处，你就必须找到一个可以看到良好教练发生的环境，并且良好教练的良好迹象实际上是一次又一次的良好结果。获胜的团队，获胜的表现，伟大的产品，伟大的产品来自伟大的产品团队。他们可能有优秀的领导者，或者在糟糕的文化中拥有优秀的领导者。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So essentially it's get a bunch of reps in is a big part of this advice. Just get reps in and I think what you just said is such an important part of it is collaborative problem solving is the key thing to look for. I was going to ask you how you recommend people get into product management. I imagine this is a very similar answer, it's just find opportunities to collaboratively problem solve.
turns.zh: 因此，本质上，让一群代表参与进来是这个建议的重要组成部分。只要让代表进来，我认为你刚才所说的非常重要，协作解决问题是要寻找的关键。我想问你如何建议人们进入产品管理。我想这是一个非常相似的答案，只是寻找合作解决问题的机会。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: That's right. And I differentiate that because there are all those guys that are the, I know I like to change a light bulb or they can walk individually or thinker and stuff and I kind of differentiate that problem solving from the people that are very good at working with other people to solve a problem. And there are so many of those pockets, you're getting reps. You've heard those who that just tell you stories of them working problem and I can see how they will help me. They know how to use data, they know how to use insights. They're not afraid of talking to people. How are you going to get those reps? Because you come into my company I ask you a question like, oh, I really don't know where do I find? But if you've done the problem solve with a team, sometimes you may not even know how to get the answer, but you know who to go to get the answer. That's a gift too.
turns.zh: 这是正确的。我之所以区分这一点，是因为我知道我喜欢更换灯泡，或者他们可以单独行走或思考者之类的东西，我将解决问题的方式与那些非常擅长与其他人合作解决问题的人区分开来。而且这些口袋有很多，你会得到代表。你听说过那些只是告诉你他们工作问题的故事的人，我可以看到他们将如何帮助我。他们知道如何使用数据，他们知道如何使用洞察力。他们不害怕与人交谈。您将如何获得这些代表？因为你来到我的公司，我会问你这样的问题，哦，我真的不知道在哪里可以找到？但如果你和一个团队一起解决问题，有时你可能甚至不知道如何得到答案，但你知道该去找谁来得到答案。这也是一份礼物。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that so much of your advice comes back to being the person that knows the most or has learned the most or even looking like they're spending the time to learn the most, which makes so much sense. The people you want to entrust are the people that happen to have the answers.
turns.zh: 我喜欢你的很多建议都回到了成为最了解或学到最多的人，甚至看起来他们花时间学习最多的人，这很有意义。你想要委托的人是那些恰好有答案的人。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: I try.
turns.zh: 我尝试一下。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And each person will know. Yeah, it just makes sense. Something else you talk about is people getting promoted too early. Leaders getting promoted too early, not doing well, they end up blaming others when really they were not actually ready for this new position. Can you talk about why you think that happens and then just how maybe as that person that might be in that position right now feeling like, oh, shit, maybe it's not my fault.
turns.zh: 每个人都会知道。是的，这很有道理。你谈论的另一件事是人们晋升得太早。领导者提拔得太早，表现不佳，最终会指责他人，而实际上他们实际上还没有准备好担任这个新职位。你能谈谈你认为为什么会发生这种情况吗？然后，也许那个人现在可能会感觉，哦，该死，也许这不是我的错。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: I don't know how to make an appeal to corporations on this one. It's a similar appeal in the light of coaching too as well. Most people are promoted to a point of incompetency or so, but I kind describe the dynamic this way. It's kind of like Lenny is a fantastic engineer. If you think about it, he wins engineer of the year awards. If you go to the office, his picture is on the wall, everybody knows him. He's feeling good. But it's like one year, two years, maybe eight years in Lenny's feeling like, am I really growing in my career? Am I really challenged in my career? He looks at the engineering career ladder. The next role from his senior engineer role is engineering manager. The leadership team, HR, they look at the same thing. That's true. We love Lenny. We don't want to lose Lenny, we need to promote him. (01:05:20): And the next step is engineering manager or product manager, manager, however, I want to use the rule here. And so, we do what? We promote Lenny. It feels good at the moment. Yeah! Congratulations on your promotion. He posts a nice post. We are like, "Yeah, we're going to keep Lenny there for long time now because he's promoted." Now, Lenny has never been a manager in his whole life. He's never interviewed people, fired people, didn't even coach people or had done any of those things directly. After a couple of months, Lenny starts to recognize an interesting pattern. Nobody's clapping for him at company meetings anymore. And sure they've taken down his picture from the world because he's no longer an engineer, he's a manager. So somebody else is now the engineer of the year, they are clapping for him in meetings. He's like, he doesn't feel recognized or seen anymore. He's just a guy now behind the scenes and that kind of thing. (01:06:10): Then in a couple of weeks go by, then they have a big engineering problem. And you know what Lenny does? He jumps in and he solves the problem. Lenny did not recognize that his job has changed. His job is no longer to solve the problem directly, but to get a team of other people good at solving problems. This is because you're a great engineer but not a good manager. This story or this dynamic I've told is probably the most common origin story of what people see or deem as micromanagement. In many cases here, this individual knows how to do engineering. They don't know how to do engineering management. They don't see the shift in their dynamic being changed. We see back patterns where it's like the second you become a manager or a leader, you cannot say things like, I don't know. I'm not sure, I need help. Who told us those things? But it's like such an expectation that our leaders must have the answers, must know the right things, must do the right things. (01:07:17): And so what do we see people do? Rather than Lenny asks for help, he goes to Google and searches how to do an interview, how to write a review. Are you seeing? He reads different articles like this one looks cool and then he does it and nobody dies. Nothing breaks so he thinks there's a good framework and a good pattern. And we have this dysfunctional culture of everybody doing different things, whatever works for anybody and that is the cycle that repeats itself. Now, a person that works for Lenny sees that he used this framework and thinks it must be a good framework, my boss did it, and you see how that cycle repeats itself? Because Lenny didn't actually get coached to be a manager. If you ask anybody that works with me, if come to me and say, "Oh, I need to get promoted to be a director." You know what I say? I say, "Go be a director. You don't need a title. Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job." You see where it falls apart in promotions? We promote people and it's like you're now a VP, do VP things. And you're like, I have never done VP things before, but I cannot tell people I've never done VP things because it makes me look incompetent, but I see the job description. I should do some VP things. What did my last VP do? Those things and those. How you say? But the best place to learn how to be a VP is when you're not a VP because that's where you practice being a VP. (01:08:52): That's where you get feedback on because then when you become a VP, you have done those things before. It's like why is the first time you've done an interview when you're now a VP? Come in and do an interview with me, observe me do an interview, ask questions, see what works, get feedback. That's why I love those group product manager roles because those are actually meant to be designed as ways for people to make a decision if they want to be a manager or they want to just stay in the discipline, but people use them as why would you give somebody four direct reports if no evidence, they can manage one? So what I do is I give you one, you might tell me, I hate people. That's okay, we can talk about that. But it's like, let me give you four and you're just going to practice the bad behavior on four. (01:09:37): So this is what often happens in company. We promote them into incompetence. It's not their fault because we are not coaching them. What we need to do is create a safe environment for people to practice leadership before they become leaders, before we promote them. We have to have good coaching programs for leaders to say, if there's a succession plan, I want Lenny to be a new manager. I don't wait till it's time to promote him then I teach him management because then apparently he cannot say things like, I don't know. I have to teach him leadership and management before he becomes a leader or a manager.
turns.zh: 我不知道如何向企业提出这一问题。从教练的角度来看，这也是类似的吸引力。大多数人都会被提升到无法胜任的程度，但我是这样描述这种动态的。莱尼就像是一位出色的工程师。如果你仔细想想，他赢得了年度工程师奖。如果你去办公室，他的照片挂在墙上，每个人都认识他。他感觉很好。但莱尼感觉好像一年，两年，也许八年，我的职业生涯真的在成长吗？我的职业生涯真的面临挑战吗？他着眼于工程职业阶梯。他的高级工程师角色的下一个角色是工程经理。领导团队、人力资源部门，他们都看同样的事情。这是真的。我们爱莱尼。我们不想失去莱尼，我们需要提升他。 (01:05:20)：下一步是工程经理或者产品经理、经理，但是，我想在这里使用这个规则。那么，我们做什么呢？我们宣传莱尼。此刻感觉很好。是的！恭喜您晋升。他发表了一篇很好的帖子。我们会说，“是的，我们要把莱尼留在那里很长时间，因为他升职了。”现在，莱尼一生都没有当过经理。他从来没有采访过人，解雇过人，甚至没有指导过人，也没有直接做过任何这些事情。几个月后，莱尼开始认识到一个有趣的模式。再也没有人在公司会议上为他鼓掌了。当然，他们已经从世界上撤下了他的照片，因为他不再是一名工程师，他是一名经理。所以现在有人成为了年度工程师，他们在会议上为他鼓掌。他感觉自己不再被认可或被看见了。他现在只是幕后的一个人而已。 (01:06:10)：几周后，他们遇到了一个很大的工程问题。你知道莱尼是做什么的吗？他跳进去解决了问题。莱尼没有意识到他的工作已经发生了变化。他的工作不再是直接解决问题，而是组建一支由善于解决问题的人组成的团队。这是因为你是一名出色的工程师，但不是一名优秀的经理。我讲述的这个故事或动态可能是人们所看到或认为的微观管理最常见的起源故事。在许多情况下，这个人知道如何进行工程设计。他们不知道如何进行工程管理。他们没有看到自己的动态发生了变化。我们看到了一些模式，就像当你成为经理或领导者时，你不能说“我不知道”之类的话。我不确定，我需要帮助。谁告诉我们这些事情的？但这就像这样一种期望，即我们的领导人必须有答案，必须知道正确的事情，必须做正确的事情。 (01:07:17)：那么我们看到人们在做什么呢？莱尼没有寻求帮助，而是去谷歌搜索如何进行采访、如何撰写评论。你看见了吗？他读了不同的文章，比如这篇看起来很酷，然后他就这么做了，没有人死。没有任何问题，所以他认为有一个好的框架和好的模式。我们有一种功能失调的文化，每个人都做不同的事情，无论对任何人都有效，这就是不断重复的循环。现在，一个为 Lenny 工作的人看到他使用了这个框架，并认为它一定是一个很好的框架，我的老板做到了，你看到这个循环是如何重复的吗？因为莱尼实际上并没有接受过教练培训。如果你问任何与我一起工作的人，如果他来对我说：“哦，我需要晋升为导演。”你知道我说什么吗？我说：“去当一名导演吧。你不需要头衔。让我告诉你导演是做什么的。在接下来的几个月里，你将和我一起做这些事情，因为我是在提升你做这份工作，而不是学习这份工作。”你知道它在促销中的失败之处吗？我们提拔员工，就像你现在是副总裁一样，做副总裁的事情。你会说，我以前从未做过副总裁的事情，但我不能告诉人们我从未做过副总裁的事情，因为这让我看起来不称职，但我看到了职位描述。我应该做一些副总裁的事情。我的上一位副总裁做了什么？那些事那些事。你说怎么样？但学习如何成为副总裁的最佳地点是当你还不是副总裁时，因为那是你练习成为副总裁的地方。 (01:08:52)：这就是您获得反馈的地方，因为当您成为副总裁时，您以前已经做过这些事情。就像你现在是副总裁时为什么第一次接受采访一样？进来接受我的采访，观察我的采访，提出问题，看看什么有效，获得反馈。这就是为什么我喜欢这些团队产品经理的角色，因为这些实际上是为了让人们做出决定，如果他们想成为一名经理，或者他们只想留在这个领域，但人们用它们来解释为什么你会给某人四个直接报告，如果没有证据，他们可以管理一个？所以我所做的就是给你一个，你可能会告诉我，我讨厌人。没关系，我们可以讨论这个。但这就像，让我给你四个，你只需在四个上练习不良行为。 (01:09:37)：这就是公司里经常发生的事情。我们将他们提升为无能。这不是他们的错，因为我们没有指导他们。我们需要做的是，在人们成为领导者之前、在我们提拔他们之前，为他们创造一个安全的领导环境。我们必须有良好的指导计划，让领导者能够说，如果有继任计划，我希望莱尼成为一名新经理。我不会等到晋升他的时候才教他管理，因为显然他不能说“我不知道”之类的话。在他成为领导者或经理之前，我必须教他领导和管理。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love this idea of just doing VP things. I just picture someone walking around and, I'm doing VP things.
turns.zh: 我喜欢只做副总裁事情的想法。我只是想象有人走来走去，而我正在做副总裁的事情。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: I'm doing VP things. All the time, I see them live, but what's a VP thing?
turns.zh: 我正在做副总裁的事情。我一直都在现场观看他们，但是 VP 是什么？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm doing VP things. I think another added benefit of doing these things before you say you're VP is that is the best way to get promoted to a VP is you are already doing the job.
turns.zh: 我正在做副总裁的事情。我认为在你成为副总裁之前做这些事情的另一个好处是，这是晋升副总裁的最佳方式，因为你已经在做这份工作了。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: That's right. And nobody bites you on it. You see that? And you're not even surprised by it and it's very safe because when you're not in the job, you can make mistakes and nobody blames you. He's not a VP, look at him trying to do VP things. You see? But the second you're a VP, there's so much leverage in the role that your mistake is serious because it impacts everybody. But when you're not, it's like you get coverage, you get protection, nobody's as mad at you. It's like, yeah, he was just trying to take a stab at it. Let's coach him on that. But what is the best time to know those things? It's before you're in it. Before you're in it
turns.zh: 这是正确的。而且没有人会咬你。你看到了吗？你甚至不会对此感到惊讶，而且它非常安全，因为当你不在工作中时，你可能会犯错误，而且没有人会责怪你。他不是副总裁，看看他试图做副总裁的事情。你看？但一旦你成为副总裁，这个角色就具有很大的影响力，你的错误会很严重，因为它会影响到每个人。但当你不这样做时，就像你得到了保险，你得到了保护，没有人对你生气。就好像，是的，他只是想尝试一下。让我们在这方面指导他。但了解这些事情的最佳时间是什么时候呢？这是在你进入其中之前。在你参与其中之前

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: To give companies and leaders something to do with this advice, you talk about helping them train and practice before they do this. How did you do that? I don't know, is it work with Silicon Valley Product Group to help train and coach?
turns.zh: 为了给公司和领导者一些建议，你谈到在他们这样做之前帮助他们进行培训和练习。你是怎么做到的？我不知道，是否与硅谷产品组合作，帮助培训和辅导？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: There are many great product coaches out there. There are many leadership coaches out there. I think there's some recognition. People have to have the humility and the self-awareness to recognize that there are opportunities for them to get better as a leader and product management, you need to see or experience, good leadership, you need the reps of good leadership and we do it in everyway. You probably talk to people about strategy and what did they do? They outsource it all the time. Tell somebody else to do it, and that cycle feeds itself because you never do it. You only know how to outsource it. You never learn how to do it. You see? And so many people outsource, oh, go get a mentor, go take a training class, and they'll think that they're outsourcing coaching in that way. It's like go take a communication.
turns.zh: 那里有很多优秀的产品教练。那里有很多领导力教练。我觉得还是有一定的认可度的人们必须有谦逊和自我意识，认识到他们有机会成为更好的领导者和产品管理人员，你需要看到或体验良好的领导力，你需要良好领导力的代表，我们在各个方面都这样做。您可能会与人们谈论战略以及他们做了什么？他们一直将其外包。告诉别人这样做，这个循环就会自行发展，因为你从来不这样做。你只知道如何外包它。你永远学不会如何去做。你看？很多人外包，哦，去找导师，去参加培训班，他们会认为他们是以这种方式外包教练的。就像去进行沟通一样。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Sourcing coaching in that way. It's like, " [inaudible 01:12:03]. Go take a communication class." I'm like, "Okay." They come back from the class, and they punch you in the face. I'm like, "Why did you punch me?" "The class taught me to punch you in the face. You paid money for me to learn how to punch you in the face." I say, go to the communication class with the employee because they're going to need to practice the communication. (01:12:20): You learn what they're learning. Both of you now will practice it together, so that they can get better at communication. A communication class doesn't get you better at communication. Communicating better is an indication that you're better at communication. You need to practice it. And I need to create a safe place for you to practice, I need to give you feedback that you're communicating better. These are all patterns in coaching that many leaders just don't have these tools and techniques to do it. (01:12:48): I do teach a lot of leaders how to coach. I do a lot of people work with leaders. There's not a singular product problem. People here me say, "All problems are people problems." There's not a singular problem that I have not seen coaching address.
turns.zh: 以这种方式寻找教练。就像，“[听不清 01:12:03]。去参加沟通课程。”我说：“好吧。”他们下课回来，就会打你的脸。我说：“你为什么打我？” “课程教我打你脸，你花钱让我学打你脸。”我说，和员工一起去参加沟通课程，因为他们需要练习沟通。 (01:12:20)：您了解他们正在学习的内容。你们现在就一起练习一下，这样他们就能更好地沟通。沟通课程并不能让你更好地沟通。更好的沟通表明你更擅长沟通。你需要练习它。我需要为你创造一个安全的练习场所，我需要给你反馈，表明你的沟通能力更好了。这些都是教练模式，许多领导者只是没有这些工具和技术来做到这一点。 (01:12:48)：我确实教过很多领导者如何指导。我确实有很多人与领导者一起工作。不存在单一的产品问题。我这里的人说：“所有问题都是人的问题。”我没有看到教练解决过任何单一问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What I hear is essentially the biggest burden is on the manager to be a great coach to their reports, and for a manager to get good at this, essentially a coach is a really good method. Bring someone in that could work with you one-on-one on a lot of these things. Awesome. That's very actionable, very solvable. (01:13:21): Everyone's always going to ask, "How do I find an awesome coach?" Difficult, I guess. I don't know. What do you tell people to go find a coach? Is there anything you could recommend, just how to go find a coach?
turns.zh: 我听到的本质上最大的负担是经理要成为他们报告的出色教练，而对于经理来说，要擅长这一点，本质上教练是一个非常好的方法。找一个可以在很多事情上与你一对一合作的人。惊人的。这是非常可行的，非常可以解决的。 (01:13:21)：每个人总是会问，“我怎样才能找到一位出色的教练？”我想，很难。我不知道。你怎么告诉人们去寻找教练？有什么可以推荐的吗，比如如何去找教练？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: You've got to find people that have generated good outcomes. People are always like, "How do you find a good consultant?" I get people teaching people a lot that haven't done the job. Don't get me wrong. If you look at American football teams, there are some coaches that have played the game before, and you feel good that they can coach you. And there are also some coaches that have not played the game, but if you look at the pedigree, they've learned from good coaches, they've worked under good coaches. (01:13:57): Same thing with product. I say there are only two parts. A good coach is someone that has played the game before and has generated good outcomes, and the second is that they've learned from good product coaches. You want to find people with a strong pedigree. You see [inaudible 01:14:12], and you, "Oh, you worked at Amazon this year," or "You worked at this company," or "You worked at Stripe. [inaudible 01:14:18] good results. How did you do that?" (01:14:19): "Oh, my environment was great. The culture was great." "Who taught you? Who coached you?" Do pick-up games with the people that they coached. They will tell you what patterns their coach told them. How do you do that? My coach told me to do this, and you're going to learn from them. I say, "Oh." Important things.
turns.zh: 你必须找到能够产生良好成果的人。人们总是会问，“你如何找到一个好的顾问？”我让人们教了很多没有完成这项工作的人。别误会我的意思。如果你看看美国橄榄球队，有一些教练以前参加过这项比赛，你会因为他们能够执教你而感到高兴。还有一些教练没有打过比赛，但如果你看看血统，他们向优秀的教练学习，他们在优秀的教练手下工作过。 (01:13:57)：产品也是如此。我说只有两部分。一个好的教练是一个以前玩过这个游戏并产生了良好结果的人，第二个是他们向好的产品教练学习。您想找到具有强大血统的人。你会看到 [听不清 01:14:12]，然后你会说，“哦，你今年在亚马逊工作”，或者“你在这家公司工作”，或者“你在 Stripe 工作。[听不清 01:14:18] 成绩不错。你是怎么做到的？” (01:14:19)：“哦，我的环境很棒。文化很棒。” “谁教你的？谁辅导你的？”与他们指导的人进行接球游戏。他们会告诉你他们的教练告诉他们的模式。你是怎么做到的？我的教练告诉我这样做，你会向他们学习。我说：“哦。”重要的事情。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Okay. Final area I want to spend a little time on is the work you do in Africa. Marty said that you're the foremost expert in introducing product and technology into world's developing countries. I know you spend a lot of time in Africa specifically. Can you just talk about the work you do there and also just maybe the opportunities and challenges you run into when you're working with folks there?
turns.zh: 惊人的。好的。我想花一点时间讨论的最后一个领域是你们在非洲所做的工作。马蒂说，您是将产品和技术引入世界发展中国家的最重要的专家。我知道您在非洲度过了很多时间。您能谈谈您在那里所做的工作以及与那里的人们一起工作时遇到的机遇和挑战吗？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Yeah. I have an African background, and my family is there, and I used to have this false notion that the things we've done in North America or Europe or Asia, the problems we've solved, have been solved in these markets. I remember talking to someone in Africa years ago, and he said to me, "Oh." I said, "You just got a new job. Where did you find a job?" He's like, "Oh, I found it in a newspaper." I said, "A newspaper? What do you mean found a job?" I remember participating in solving that exact problem in 1998. I was working with the team to solve that, and I had this false assumption that because I solved it here, of course it's solved everywhere. (01:15:40): I started to see patterns like this in Africa where just two things were trending. One, so many, the poor use of technology and enabling technologies to solve problems. And two, the difficulty in actually solving problems in these markets, in these emerging markets. And one of the things we take for granted, I always tell people the government is probably the biggest public private product platform in the world. In all countries, they all have this public... Because they provide the infrastructure and the architecture that is enabling for people. (01:16:18): Imagine if you were trying to code and you didn't have power. Now you're thinking there are markets where you have to solve the problem of getting power before you then getting access to a computer and then getting access to the right type of software to be able to code something. Look at all the different things. You have to solve many problems just before you can start to solve the problem in a meaningful way. This is a very big reflection of the dynamic in Africa. (01:16:44): The second pattern of what we see is because of this challenge, I see two things. One, people make a lot of money on a problem than from solving the problem. There's this whole society that people are very good at walking around problems. "We've got an electricity problem, we'll just buy generators." "We've got a road problem, we're going to buy bigger cars." I was talk at a conference, and I was driving up to it, and I saw a Tesla with a portable generator at the back of it. They'll stop and charge the Tesla, and they keep going on the road. In some ways, that's a whole society, but it's never been a society that didn't have creative people. (01:17:26): Just an amazing, tremendous amount of talent. It's a very young population. I talk to people all the time. I say, "Look." Someone told me, "Well, Africa, seven of the eight most underdeveloped places in the world are in Africa." (01:17:41): And I said, "Well." They were talking about the discovery of the internet. Less than 30% of Africa has discovered the internet. And I tell them, "Wow. And we created seven Unicoms from that. Imagine if 50%, 75% discovered the internet. We need to understand the opportunities, the youngest population, the fastest growing, some of the fastest growing economies in these markets. Some of the problems are so basic, and the opportunities are so huge. So I had to kill all these assumptions. One, that I needed permission to come to solve problems there, and two, that we didn't have the means to equip and educate people. (01:18:24): We don't have a talent problem or a resource problem. The biggest opportunity I've found is to really empower a continent with enabling technology and the mindset and the skills to be able to leverage technology in solving problems. (01:18:40): This led to me starting a nonprofit in Africa, the Innovate Africa Foundation, and we are committed to this education of people on the continent, this enablement with technology. We did our first conference last year, the Inspire Africa Conference. It just blew my mind. I'm so humbled when I could see a thousand people from 31 different countries in Africa come with a hunger and an eagerness to learn how to do product work. And it's not cheap by any means for them to do that. (01:19:14): What moved me the most is looking at the future generation. We had a 13-year-old and an 11-year-old in the workshop. The 11-year-old was a robotics engineer. The 13-year-old was a CEO of a small startup that keeps healthcare records, a leader. And I'm like, "If I can help these people learn how to do product well, this is the whole generation for Africa. This is the future of people that want to leverage technology in a meaningful way." So I spend a lot of my time in Africa, coaching, advising and teaching teams how to use technology, how to do product, how to organize themselves as product teams, how to solve problems, and really to create a boldness within the continent for them to go after problems and solve them, than walk around the problems or make money on them.
turns.zh: 是的。我有非洲背景，我的家人在那里，我曾经有一种错误的观念，认为我们在北美、欧洲或亚洲所做的事情，我们解决的问题，已经在这些市场得到解决。我记得几年前在非洲与某人交谈，他对我说：“哦。”我说：“你刚刚找到了一份新工作，你在哪里找到的工作？”他说：“哦，我在报纸上找到的。”我说：“报纸？你说找到工作是什么意思？”我记得在 1998 年参与解决这个问题。我正在与团队合作解决这个问题，我有一个错误的假设，因为我在这里解决了这个问题，当然它在任何地方都得到了解决。 (01:15:40)：我开始在非洲看到这样的模式，那里只有两种趋势。一是技术和解决问题的技术使用不当。第二，在这些新兴市场中实际解决问题的难度。我们认为理所当然的一件事是，我总是告诉人们政府可能是世界上最大的公共私营产品平台。在所有国家，他们都有这样的公共......因为他们提供了为人们提供支持的基础设施和架构。 (01:16:18)：想象一下，如果您尝试编码但没有电源。现在您正在考虑在某些市场中，您必须先解决获得电力的问题，然后才能访问计算机，然后访问正确类型的软件才能编写代码。看看所有不同的事情。在你开始以有意义的方式解决问题之前，你必须先解决许多问题。这在很大程度上反映了非洲的动态。 (01:16:44)：我们看到的第二种模式是因为这个挑战，我看到了两件事。第一，人们在解决问题上赚到的钱比解决问题赚的钱多。整个社会的人们都非常善于解决问题。 “我们遇到了电力问题，我们就买发电机。” “我们遇到了道路问题，我们要购买更大的汽车。”我在一次会议上演讲，当我开车去那里时，我看到一辆特斯拉，后面有一个便携式发电机。他们会停下来给特斯拉充电，然后继续上路。从某些方面来说，这就是一个完整的社会，但它从来都不是一个没有创造力的人的社会。 (01:17:26)：才华横溢，令人惊叹。这是一个非常年轻的群体。我一直与人交谈。我说：“看。”有人告诉我，“嗯，非洲，世界上八个最不发达的地方中有七个在非洲。” (01:17:41)：我说：“好吧。”他们正在谈论互联网的发现。不到 30% 的非洲人发现了互联网。我告诉他们，“哇。我们由此创建了七个联通公司。想象一下，如果 50%、75% 的人发现了互联网。我们需要了解这些市场中的机会、最年轻的人口、增长最快的经济体。有些问题非常基本，而机会却如此巨大。所以我必须放弃所有这些假设。第一，我需要获得许可才能去那里解决问题，第二，我们没有能力装备和教育人们。 (01:18:24)：我们没有人才问题或资源问题。我发现的最大机会是真正为非洲大陆提供支持技术以及能够利用技术解决问题的技能。(01:18:40)：这促使我在非洲创办了一个非营利组织——创新非洲基金会，我们致力于对非洲大陆的人们进行教育，这是我们去年举办的第一次会议，即“激励非洲”。当我看到来自非洲 31 个不同国家的 1000 个人充满渴望和渴望学习如何进行产品工作时，我感到非常震惊（01:19:14）：最让我感动的是我们的下一代。 11 岁。这位 13 岁的年轻人是一家保存医疗记录的小型初创公司的首席执行官，也是一名领导者，“如果我能帮助这些人学习如何做好产品，这就是整个非洲的一代。这是希望以有意义的方式利用技术的人们的未来。”因此，我在非洲花费了大量时间，指导、建议和教导团队如何使用技术、如何做产品、如何将自己组织为产品团队、如何解决问题，并真正在非洲大陆创造一种勇气，让他们去追寻问题并解决问题，而不是绕过问题或利用问题赚钱。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: If people want to learn more about this, maybe support the work you're doing, what's the best way to find out more?
turns.zh: 如果人们想了解更多相关信息，或者支持您正在做的工作，那么了解更多信息的最佳方式是什么？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: You can visit the nonprofit website. It's innovateafricafoundation.org. You can follow our work on SVPG or the inspireafricaconference.com. I know I will be doing a lot more next year. In January, I am going to be launching a fund, the Paid Africa Fund, and I want it to be a fund funded by the product community for Africa. It's an angel investment fund. One of the problems I recognize is that so many of the startups, they are not ready for institutional investment, and they are forced into it in some ways. They say people are giving up a lot of equity when they just need cashflow. And so I really want to focus on a fund for the community to enable people to get product market fit in those markets. (01:20:55): That'll be launching in January. I'll probably do an announcement about it. I'm excited about that work and to really try to promote more of product-centric thinking on the continent.
turns.zh: 您可以访问非营利网站。这是 Innovationafricafoundation.org。您可以在 SVPG 或 informafricaconference.com 上关注我们的工作。我知道明年我会做更多的事情。一月份，我将推出一项基金，即付费非洲基金，我希望它成为由非洲产品社区资助的基金。这是一个天使投资基金。我认识到的问题之一是，很多初创公司还没有准备好接受机构投资，并且在某些方面被迫参与。他们说，当人们只需要现金流时，他们就会放弃大量股权。因此，我真的想专注于社区基金，使人们能够获得适合这些市场的产品。 (01:20:55)：将于一月份推出。我可能会就此发布一个公告。我对这项工作感到很兴奋，并真正尝试在非洲大陆推广更多以产品为中心的思维。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. You should call this fun reference customers or something along those lines, if the goal is to help them find product market [inaudible 01:21:12]-
turns.zh: 惊人的。如果目标是帮助他们找到产品市场，您应该将其称为有趣的参考客户或类似的名称 [听不清 01:21:12]-

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: That's right. They'll be learning a lot of that.
turns.zh: 这是正确的。他们会学到很多东西。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Christian, is there anything else you wanted to share or leave listeners with before we get to our very exciting lightning round?
turns.zh: 克里斯蒂安，在我们开始激动人心的闪电回合之前，您还有什么想与听众分享或留给听众的吗？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: I've always made an appeal to the product community to really have a sense of what they do beyond the job of a products team or product manager. And I always try to encourage people to see that: at the very core of what you do is really solving a problem. And that's creating... When you do that, create value in the world, you're making a dent in the world. People that participate in trying to make things better or trying to solve problems, and we should not shy from that definition of our job. (01:21:58): It might feel like a fluffy one. It might feel too lightweight and not meaningful, but I think when people take to heart that that's really what the essence of products is or product work is, they bring to work a different passion, they bring to work a different sense of empathy, they bring to work a different sense of customer centricity. And all of those things lead to good outcomes. (01:22:21): I always make that appeal to product people as like, "Yeah, all the frameworks, techniques, all the stuff, just think truly about what you're trying to do. You're trying to care enough about a problem to solve it on someone's behalf and do it so well that it give us something every time."
turns.zh: 我一直呼吁产品社区真正了解他们在产品团队或产品经理的工作之外所做的事情。我总是试图鼓励人们看到这一点：你所做的事情的核心是真正解决问题。这就是创造……当你这样做时，为世界创造价值，你就在世界上留下了印记。人们参与努力让事情变得更好或试图解决问题，我们不应该回避我们工作的定义。 (01:21:58)：它可能感觉像一个蓬松的。它可能感觉太轻量且没有意义，但我认为当人们牢记这才是产品或产品工作的本质时，他们会给工作带来不同的热情，他们会给工作带来不同的同理心，他们会给工作带来不同的以客户为中心的感觉。所有这些都会带来好的结果。 (01:22:21)：我总是向产品人员发出这样的呼吁，“是的，所有的框架、技术，所有的东西，只要认真思考你想要做什么。你试图足够关心一个问题，以代表某人解决它，并且做得很好，每次都会给我们带来一些东西。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I really love that last point of just that's how you know if you've built something people care about. They give you something in return, and one of those things could be actually telling other people about it.
turns.zh: 我真的很喜欢最后一点，这就是你如何知道你是否构建了人们关心的东西。他们会给你一些回报，其中之一可能就是实际告诉其他人。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: That's right.
turns.zh: 这是正确的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: To your point about reference customers.
turns.zh: 关于参考客户的观点。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Well, with that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 惊人的。好了，至此，我们已经进入了非常激动人心的闪电回合。你准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: I don't have a choice.
turns.zh: 我别无选择。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Nope. What are two or three books that you've recommended most to other people?
turns.zh: 没有。您向其他人推荐最多的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Oh boy. In this discipline, probably all of our books: Inspired, Empowered, and we are coming up with one in March, Transformed.
turns.zh: 噢，孩子。在这个学科中，可能我们所有的书：《灵感》、《赋权》，我们将在三月份推出一本《转型》。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I see that tee shirt there. I see the promo happening.
turns.zh: 我看到那里的那件 T 恤。我看到促销活动正在发生。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Yes, it's happening. It's happening. But it's really a reflection of so many decades of love and passion for product work. And I have not found, I always told Maddie that you write the books after have gone through the failure. It's like, "I've failed at leadership, now there's a book on it. I've failed at product, now there's a book on it." And it reflects really the heart of good product work. I love Ben said the hard thing about hard things I love. There's some books that really describe the mindset and culture that good product work is done in. I always recommend those to people.
turns.zh: 是的，它正在发生。它正在发生。但这确实反映了几十年来对产品工作的热爱和热情。我还没有发现，我总是告诉麦迪，你在经历了失败之后才写书。就像是，“我在领导力方面失败了，现在有一本关于它的书。我在产品方面失败了，现在有一本关于它的书。”它真正反​​映了优秀产品工作的核心。我喜欢本对我喜欢的困难的事情说了困难的话。有一些书真正描述了优秀产品工作的心态和文化。我总是向人们推荐这些书。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just on this topic of Transformed while we're on it, when is it coming out, and can you give just an elevator pitch for the book just so people know what it'll be about?
turns.zh: 就在我们正在讨论的《Transformed》这个主题上，它什么时候出版？你能为这本书做一个电梯推介，以便人们知道它会讲什么吗？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Transformed is coming out March next year. Oh God, just three months. Some people should have gotten shipping dates on their books if you pre-ordered it now. But it really talks about how to move to the product model or the product operating model, which is really this set of beliefs and principles that the best companies work in. We share stories of companies that have transformed into this that are not your traditional bond digital or bond tech companies that have made this transition. We tell stories of what companies can do. If it's anything, it's an appeal that there is a better way of working and solving problems and that companies can work in this way regardless of where you are in the journey.
turns.zh: 《Transformed》将于明年三月上映。天哪，才三个月。如果你现在预订的话，有些人应该已经在他们的书上找到了发货日期。但它真正讨论的是如何转向产品模式或产品运营模式，这实际上是最好的公司所遵循的这套信念和原则。我们分享已经转型为这种模式的公司的故事，这些公司不是传统的债券数字或债券科技公司，而是进行了这种转型。我们讲述公司可以做什么的故事。如果有的话，那就是呼吁有更好的工作和解决问题的方式，并且无论你处于旅程的哪个阶段，公司都可以以这种方式工作。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: All right. We'll have to have you back once the book comes out to get more people aware of what is happening. Amazing. Okay, I'll keep going. Favorite recent movie or TV show that you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 好的。一旦这本书出版，我们就必须让你回来，让更多的人知道正在发生的事情。惊人的。好吧，我会继续。您最近最喜欢的最喜欢的电影或电视节目？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: I jumped on the Succession bandwagon, and I enjoyed, and I used to love Billions too as well. I love good writing, really just intellectual media writing business. And so probably Succession and Billions would be two.
turns.zh: 我加入了继任者的行列，我很喜欢，而且我也曾经很喜欢《十亿》。我喜欢好的写作，实际上只是智力媒体写作业务。所以《继任者》和《十亿》可能是两个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite interview question that you like to ask when you're interviewing candidates?
turns.zh: 当你面试候选人时，你有最喜欢问的面试问题吗？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Well, I always give them a problem to solve. That is probably my favorite question, and it's not a traditional problem. I probably will see something like, "Hey Lenny, I have a friend. He's been legally deaf or hearing impaired his whole life, and he just got a new job that requires him to wake up significantly earlier than he normally does. And as you can imagine, traditional alarm clocks will not do it, will not solve the problem. And I would love to give that problem to you. Walk me through how you go about tackling this or solving this." For me, I like that question because it gives me a sense of how you think. It gives me a sense of how you solve problems. It gives me a sense of how you know what you do not know and how you go about knowing the things you need to know, what you need to solve a problem. (01:25:52): There's no magical right or wrong answer. I do a lot of people that say, "I have no clue what to do. I'm more curious and because I want to now know what you do, but you don't have a clue." Or people that jump straight to solutions, are more engineering-centric. People that jump straight to... I can get a sense of who you are when I give you a problem that requires you to do some thinking.
turns.zh: 嗯，我总是给他们一个需要解决的问题。这可能是我最喜欢的问题，而且它不是一个传统问题。我可能会看到这样的内容：“嘿，莱尼，我有一个朋友。他一生都是法定聋人或听力障碍，而他刚刚找到了一份新工作，要求他比平时早起很多。正如你所想象的，传统的闹钟不会做到这一点，不会解决问题。我很乐意把这个问题交给你。告诉我你如何处理这个问题或解决这个问题。”对我来说，我喜欢这个问题，因为它让我了解你的想法。它让我了解你如何解决问题。它让我了解你如何知道你不知道的事情，以及你如何了解你需要知道的事情，以及解决问题所需的内容。 (01:25:52)：没有神奇的正确或错误答案。我遇到很多人说：“我不知道该怎么做。我更好奇，因为我现在想知道你在做什么，但你不知道。”或者直接跳到解决方案的人更以工程为中心。当我给你一个需要你思考的问题时，我可以了解你是谁。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And you're doing this live in an interview? It's not like, "Go home and think about this, and then-
turns.zh: 你是在现场采访中这样做的吗？这并不是说，“回家想想这个，然后——

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Oh, I'm doing this live in an interview.
turns.zh: 哦，我是在采访中现场直播的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Live, okay. And then what's a sign that they're on the right track? What do you look for that's like, "Yes, this is what I want to see"?
turns.zh: 活着，还好吧。那么什么迹象表明他们走在正确的轨道上呢？你在寻找什么就像“是的，这就是我想看到的”？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Remember, when I think about what makes a good product manager, I look about collaborative problem solving. There are people that feel like, I'm just going to solve the whole thing myself. This is what we should do. We should do it like no evidence, no data, no kind of stuff in there. It's very interesting. But people that are saying, "You know what? I would need probably work an engineer and designer. We might need to put [inaudible 01:26:46]." I look for intellectual curiosity in some ways, people that have proven questions in your head. People that are very quick to see things [inaudible 01:26:54] people. I will talk to 20 of them. I say, "How you going to do that? Do you know sign language?" And they're like, "Oh, how am I going to talk to them?" There are people that are like, "I'm going to need a lot of help to try to figure this out. I don't know a lot about your friend, but I know..." Some people have frameworks they run to. It exposes that, if they're married to one way of working. (01:27:14): It's more about knowing what you can't know. I'm looking for empathy, humility in some sense. It is a competence thing because most of I can teach, I can coach a lot of things, but that arrogance, that ego, those kinds of things, those "I walk alone," those things are very, very challenging and disruptive to a team culture.
turns.zh: 请记住，当我思考如何成为一名优秀的产品经理时，我会考虑协作解决问题。有些人觉得，我要自己解决整个问题。这是我们应该做的。我们应该像没有证据、没有数据、没有任何东西一样去做。这很有趣。但人们会说，“你知道吗？我可能需要担任一名工程师和设计师。我们可能需要添加 [听不清 01:26:46]。”我以某种方式寻找求知欲，那些在你头脑中证明了问题的人。那些能很快看到事物的人 [听不清 01:26:54] 人们。我将与其中 20 个人交谈。我说：“你打算怎么做？你懂手语吗？”他们会说，“哦，我该怎么跟他们说话呢？”有些人会说，“我需要很多帮助才能解决这个问题。我对你的朋友不太了解，但我知道......”有些人有他们所使用的框架。如果他们只选择一种工作方式，就会暴露这一点。 (01:27:14)：更重要的是了解你所不知道的事情。我正在寻找某种意义上的同理心和谦逊。这是一个能力问题，因为我可以教大多数人，我可以指导很多事情，但是傲慢，自我，诸如此类的事情，那些“我独自行走”，这些事情对团队文化来说非常非常具有挑战性和破坏性。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite product that you've recently discovered that you really like? Either an app or something physical? Anything that's like, "Oh, this is really cool"?
turns.zh: 您最近发现有您真正喜欢的最喜欢的产品吗？是应用程序还是实体？有什么类似“哦，这真的很酷”的事情吗？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: My eldest son is into sports. He loves all kinds of sports stuff, sports apps, all of those kinds of things, and he got me on this app called Real, like real sports. It's really cool. It shows scores of different games, but it's really driven by social influence. So all of your Twitter posts will get there like, "Oh my God, [inaudible 01:28:07]." It's almost like real time more than real time. You're getting real time with reactions of people around you and your communities. (01:28:15): It's a very different way of checking on a score than I've ever seen, and I thought it was just really, really thoughtful in how... I want to share reaction to touchdown with 50 people around the world that will care about my favorite team just got a touchdown, and you'll all share reactions at the same time. And the first person that saw it, you can see it. It's very simple. This is like scores for games, but these days I don't check my scores anywhere else but on it.
turns.zh: 我的大儿子喜欢运动。他喜欢各种体育用品、体育应用程序，所有这些东西，他让我使用了这个名为 Real 的应用程序，就像真正的体育运动一样。真的很酷。它显示了不同游戏的分数，但它实际上是由社会影响力驱动的。所以你所有的 Twitter 帖子都会像这样：“天哪，[听不清 01:28:07]”。这几乎比实时更接近实时。您可以实时了解周围人和社区的反应。 (01:28:15)：这是一种与我见过的非常不同的检查得分的方式，我认为这真的非常非常周到……我想与世界各地 50 个人分享对触地得分的反应，他们会关心我最喜欢的球队刚刚触地得分，你们都会同时分享反应。第一个看到它的人，你就能看到它。这很简单。这就像游戏的分数，但现在我除了在上面之外不再在其他地方检查我的分数。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite life motto that you often repeat to yourself, share with friends, either in work or in life, that you find useful?
turns.zh: 您是否有一条最喜欢的人生格言，无论是在工作中还是在生活中，您经常对自己重复、与朋友分享，并且觉得有用？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Wow, boy. I've said a lot in this talk about companies don't care about about you, people care about you. It's never too late to be what you want to be. But early on, my father would always tell me, "Show up. Show up, and you're ahead of 80% of the people in the free world. Show up on time, and you're ahead of 85% of the people in the free world. Show up on time with a plan, and you're ahead of 90% of the people in the free world. And if somehow you have the guts to put that plan to action with a smile, then you probably will have a great chance of success. And if you do that over and over again, every aspect of your life, it can at least lead to successful outcomes." And I think that's a lot of some mental definition for me every day.
turns.zh: 哇，男孩。我在这次演讲中说了很多，公司不关心你，人们关心你。成为你想成为的人，永远不会太晚。但在早期，我父亲总是告诉我，“出现。出现，你就领先于自由世界 80% 的人。准时出现，你就领先于自由世界 85% 的人。按时带着计划出现，你就领先于自由世界 90% 的人。如果你有勇气微笑着把这个计划付诸行动，那么你可能会有很大的成功机会。如果你一遍又一遍地这样做，在你生活的各个方面，它至少可以带来成功的结果。”我认为这对我来说每天都有很多心理定义。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. I love that. Final question: as maybe the most interesting man in the world, is there anything people may not know about you or would be surprised to hear about?
turns.zh: 惊人的。我喜欢那个。最后一个问题：作为可能是世界上最有趣的人，有什么关于你的事情人们可能不知道或者会感到惊讶吗？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Wow. I hope there are no surprises about me in that kind of case in that way, but I went to a gifted and talented school. I was out of my house at 12, and I went to kind of boarding school, and I've never been back home since then, so I've kind of been on my own. But we are kind of in the middle of nowhere, probably eight miles from any form of civilization and stuff in the middle of the jungle. No potable water, no electricity. So you kind of had to get water yourself, generate your own power. Probably the most interesting time in my life to shape my worldview, surviving at 12 to 16 on my own in the middle of the jungle. Very intriguing part of my life.
turns.zh: 哇。我希望在这种情况下我不会感到惊讶，但我去了一所有天赋的学校。我12岁时就离开了家，去了一所寄宿学校，从那以后我就再也没有回过家，所以我一直都是靠自己。但我们有点偏僻，距离任何形式的文明和丛林中的东西可能有八英里。没有饮用水，没有电。所以你必须自己取水，自己发电。 12 岁到 16 岁的时候，我独自在丛林中生存，这可能是我一生中塑造世界观最有趣的时光。我生活中非常有趣的一部分。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Very different from your life these days. Actually, one more question. I think you're the fourth... You're from Nigeria, right? Your family's from Nigeria?
turns.zh: 与你现在的生活非常不同。其实还有一个问题。我想你是第四个......你来自尼日利亚，对吧？你的家人来自尼日利亚？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You're the fourth Nigerian guest on this podcast, I realized. And I always like to ask, what's your favorite Nigerian food slash which food should people seek out if they were to try to find some good Nigerian food?
turns.zh: 我意识到，你是这个播客的第四位尼日利亚嘉宾。我总是想问，你最喜欢的尼日利亚食物是什么？如果人们想要寻找一些好的尼日利亚食物，他们应该寻找哪些食物？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: My favorite Nigerian is super-duper cultural and native. It's like starch and [inaudible 01:31:06] soup. You can't really find that anywhere, it got to come from mom's cooking. Marty Cagan has tried it. He came to my hometown, my parents' house and had it. But if you are discovering Nigerian food, [inaudible 01:31:18] is a variation of rice, which everybody has, jollof rice, and yes people, I'm going to say this: jollof rice, Nigerian jollof is better than Ghanaian jollof. It's a war, but it's okay. We already claim victory, and we'll move on. But start with jollof rice is elementary, but then you have to try [inaudible 01:31:34] like a pounded yam with a soup. There are many different variations of that. And you get a pounded yam, like pounded cassava, and you eat that with a soup, and you will love it.
turns.zh: 我最喜欢的尼日利亚人是超级文化和本土人。它就像淀粉和 [听不清 01:31:06] 汤。你在任何地方都找不到它，它一定是妈妈做的菜。马蒂·凯根已经尝试过了。他来到我的家乡，我父母家并拥有了它。但如果您发现尼日利亚食物，[听不清 01:31:18] 是大米的一种变体，每个人都有，jollof 米饭，是的，我要说的是：jollof 米饭，尼日利亚 jollof 比加纳 jollof 更好。这是一场战争，但没关系。我们已经宣布胜利，我们将继续前进。但从 jollof 米饭开始是基本的，但随后你必须尝试 [听不清 01:31:34] 就像捣碎的山药加汤一样。有许多不同的变体。你会得到捣碎的山药，就像捣碎的木薯一样，你把它和汤一起吃，你会喜欢它的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Some controversy over here, competition-
turns.zh: 这里有些争议，竞争-

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: That's right.
turns.zh: 这是正确的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... for who's got the best rice. Amazing. Christian, I am now a huge fan of yours. I'm so happy we did this. Thank you so much for making time for this. Two final questions: where can folks find you online if they want to reach out, and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: ...谁有最好的大米。惊人的。克里斯蒂安，我现在是你的超级粉丝。我很高兴我们做到了这一点。非常感谢您抽出时间来做这件事。最后两个问题：如果人们想要联系您，可以在哪里找到您？听众如何对您有用？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: You can find me on LinkedIn as well. You can reach out to us on our websites svpg.com. I tell people the best fit to be useful to us is to do good work using these principles and all the things we teach people over and over again. We care about outcomes, we care about good product work in the world. I would love your support with the work I'm doing in Africa. I've always reached out to the product community around the world to help developing countries and communities. So please follow our work, please support our work in Africa in building a product community.
turns.zh: 您也可以在 LinkedIn 上找到我。您可以通过我们的网站 svpg.com 与我们联系。我告诉人们，最适合对我们有用的就是利用这些原则以及我们一遍又一遍教给人们的所有东西来做好工作。我们关心结果，我们关心世界上良好的产品工作。我希望得到您对我在非洲所做的工作的支持。我一直与世界各地的产品社区联系，以帮助发展中国家和社区。所以请关注我们的工作，请支持我们在非洲建立产品社区的工作。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And what is the website for that again? Specifically the nonprofit you started?
turns.zh: 那么这个网站是什么？具体来说是您创办的非营利组织？

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Innovateafricafoundation.org.
turns.zh: Innovateafricafoundation.org。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Christian, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 惊人的。克里斯蒂安，非常感谢你来到这里。

turns.speaker: Christian Idiodi
turns.en: Thank you for having me, Lenny. Such a pleasure.
turns.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，莱尼。真是太高兴了。

turns.zh: 再见，大家。非常感谢您的聆听。如果您发现这很有价值，您可以在 Apple Podcasts、Spotify 或您最喜欢的播客应用程序上订阅该节目。另外，请考虑给我们评分或留下评论，因为这确实有助于其他听众找到播客。您可以在 lennyspodcast.com 上找到所有过去的剧集或了解有关该节目的更多信息。下一集见。
